pending_commit.commit_message: crash: Add core_collector The ARC build of crash_reporter will delegate to a child core_collector process for ARC crashes. Unlike core2md, core_collector writes a stripped core dump by parsing the input stream from the kernel, which saves disk space for large ARC dumps. Note that coredump_writer.{h,cc} were ported from Ryu's crash_collector. A separate process is needed because Breakpad is dependent on word size, so crash_reporter will dispatch to a 32-bit or 64-bit variant on x86-64. The build configuration for this will be added in a subsequent CL. UPSTREAM: mwifiex: claim sdio bus while downloading the firmware Our 8887 A2 chip can have separate firmware images for bluetooth and WLAN. We observed an issue during parallel downloading of these images by btmrvl and mwifiex drivers. This patch claims sdio bus before starting of the firmware download in mwifiex and releases it after completion to fix the problem. Relax the restriction and permit read/write access on dma-buf This patch relax the restriction and permit read/write access on dma-buf. In particular this is necessary for the userspace mmap()ing a dma-buf fd, so Chrome could now use it for unpriviledged Renderers write into a graphics buffer without much difficulty. permission_broker: allow detaching whitelisted USB devices Add a new rule result ALLOW_WITH_DETACH. The DBus CheckPathAccess method would consider ALLOW_WITH_DETACH as a success. The DBus OpenPath method will detach all the interfaces of the device from the kernel if the rule processing has returned ALLOW_WITH_DETACH. Modify the DenyClaimedUsbDeviceRule rule so when its finding that the USB device has one of its interfaces claimed, it would check in the device settings (through libbrillo device_policy functions) if the USB device (actually its VID:PID pair) is whitelisted for this machine. If so, it would return ALLOW_WITH_DETACH, else it would return DENY or ALLOW_WITH_LOCKDOWN as usual. Before effectively detaching the kernel driver, the path is still checked against the existing set of rules, only the result of DenyClaimedUsbDevice is skipped for whitelisted devices. RF: refactor rf utils This module contains functions that shouldn't be here. Details below: IsInRange(): This function has no reason to exist if all GetPower() kind functions comply with the following rules: 1. In normal cases, it returns a float (excluding -inf and inf). 2. When it needs to set "no threshold", return -inf or inf, where -inf stands for "no min threshold" and inf stands for "no max threshold". 3. When it has problem returning a number, it returns NaN. For example, when reading a value from the tester, the tester may not return a valid number. In this case, something is wrong with the tester, and the caller is responsible of dealing with such error before doing the comparison (reset the tester, show error message to the user, etc.). The caller should not count on a compare function to find the error. When all these rules are satisfied by all GetPower() kind functions, we can simply write "min_threshold <= power <= max_threshold" and omit this function. FormattedPower(): Any power variable should never be None so we shouldn't have to deal with this case. The only time a power variable may be None, is after reading a config file, and before converting it to a power value. Say, if we define None as "no threshold" in the config file. It should be converted to -inf or inf immediately after reading it. (But strictly speaking, the variable at that time is still a string, not a power value.) CheckPower(): The utility module shouldn't contain anything related to "view" such as printing error message or even building error messages. DownloadParameters(): Apparently this function shouldn't be here, it should be moved to the shopfloor helper or somewhere like that.
